c.tagline: Ancient Aztec roots beneath vibrant sprawling metropolis.

emergency.note: 911 is the single nationwide emergency number; English-speaking operators are limited, and Locatel (55 5658 1111) offers city assistance.

hood_landmark.Condesa: Parque México's leafy Art Deco promenades
hood_landmark.Roma: Plaza Río de Janeiro with its David replica and café-lined Álvaro Obregón
hood_landmark.Centro Historico: the Zócalo plaza and Metropolitan Cathedral

avoid.reason: Avoid Tepito and the Doctores neighbourhood — high street crime.
Caution in the historic centre after dark and in Iztapalapa; use registered taxis/rideshare, not street cabs.

hood_desc: Condesa is a leafy, bohemian-chic district of Art Deco buildings, tree-lined avenues and buzzing sidewalk cafes and bars, ideal for younger travelers and digital nomads who want walkable nightlife and green parks.

Roma is a stylish, artsy neighborhood of restored mansions, indie galleries, specialty coffee and acclaimed restaurants, suiting foodies and creatives who want hip energy with a slightly more grown-up edge than Condesa.

Polanco is Mexico City's upscale, polished quarter of luxury hotels, designer boutiques on Avenida Presidente Masaryk and fine dining, best for affluent travelers and business visitors wanting comfort and safety.

Coyoacan is a charming, historic colonial village with cobblestone streets, plazas, markets and the Frida Kahlo house, appealing to culture lovers and families who prefer a slower, bohemian and authentically Mexican atmosphere.

Centro Historico is the dense, monumental old core around the Zocalo, packed with cathedrals, museums, ruins and street life, perfect for first-time visitors and history buffs who want to be steps from the main sights.

water.note: Avoid tap water; drink bottled or purified water, and confirm ice is made from purified water.

transit.pay: You need the rechargeable MI (Movilidad Integrada) card - paper tickets were discontinued in 2024. It costs MXN 15 (~US$0.80) plus fare balance, sold at metro station ticket booths (cash) and Metrobus/Cablebus vending machines, and works across the metro, Metrobus, Cablebus, light rail and trolleybuses. Rides are cheap: Metro MXN 5 (~US$0.25), Metrobus MXN 6.
transit.hours: Metro runs 5am-midnight weekdays, from 6am Saturdays and 7am Sundays/holidays; Metrobus Line 1 runs nearly 24 hours but most lines stop around midnight.
